Formation equilibrium  
CaY²⁻ ⇌ Ca²⁺ + Y⁴⁻

Given  
K_f = 5 × 10¹⁰  (formation constant)  
K_d = 1 / K_f = 2 × 10⁻¹¹  (dissociation constant)  
Stoichiometric (total) concentrations:  
[Ca]ₜ = [EDTA]ₜ = 0.020 M

Let x = [Ca²⁺] that is released by dissociation.

At equilibrium  
[Ca²⁺] = x  
[Y⁴⁻]   = x  
[CaY²⁻] = 0.020 − x

Apply K_d :  
K_d = [Ca²⁺][Y⁴⁻] / [CaY²⁻]  
2 × 10⁻¹¹ = x² / (0.020 − x)

Because K_d is very small, x ≪ 0.020; hence 0.020 − x ≈ 0.020.

x² = (2 × 10⁻¹¹)(0.020)  
x² = 4 × 10⁻¹³  
x  = √(4 × 10⁻¹³)  
x  ≈ 6.3 × 10⁻⁷ M

Thus  
[Ca²⁺] ≈ 6.3 × 10⁻⁷ M.

Answer: D
